question: ADOPTION item 14: does the rejected-edit memory (rejected_recent in the proposal context) stop repeat proposals on a live model?
design: OpenEvolve function-minimization task (Apache-2.0 port), two independent workspaces: rejected_memory = true (default) vs false; GLM-5.3-Flash, seed 0, 5 attempts each, frozen final test
finding: Null result on the hypothesized failure mode: GLM-5.3-Flash produced no identical or near-identical (Jaccard >= 0.6) repeat proposals in either arm at this scale, so the memory's trigger never fired. Both arms still evolved successfully (candidates 0.9944/0.9997 vs baseline 0.9418). The memory stays on by default as a zero-observed-cost safeguard; the toggle [proposer] rejected_memory is shipped.
limits: One task, one model, one seed, five attempts per arm; zero observed repeats means no power to detect a reduction. Fixture-level plumbing was validated separately (memoryless scripted proposer 2/2 repeats vs memory-aware 0/2).
